title: Snap Soars 7% as Deutsche Bank Says Its Subscription Story Is “Better Than the Tape Suggests”
detail:
Snap Soars 7% as Deutsche Bank Says Its Subscription Story Is “Better Than the Tape Suggests”
David Hanson

SNAP
META
RDDT

Trading disclosure
Snap Soars 7% as Deutsche Bank Says Its Subscription Story Is "Better Than the Tape Suggests" ©Marcela Ruth Romero from Ruty Romero's Images and mohamed abdelghaffar from Pexels via Canva
Key Takeaways

Snap shares rose 7% after Deutsche Bank kept its Buy rating and $8 target, saying investors underrate its subscriptions.

Paid subscribers rose 77% to about 30 million last quarter, bringing in about three-quarters of Snap's added revenue.

Meta Platforms, Pinterest and Reddit all grew revenue far faster than Snap's ads, so the slowdown looks like Snap's own.

The stock looks cheap on forward earnings, though those exclude about $1 billion a year of stock pay.

Snap (SNAP:NYSE) shares are up 7% today, after Deutsche Bank's Benjamin Black argued last week's post-earnings selloff missed what's driving the business. His Nov. 10 note is titled "Better Than the Tape Suggests; Subs Mix and Earnings Power Matter."

Reddit (RDDT:NYSE) is up 7% too. But the note goes straight at Snap's weak spot: its ad business barely grew last quarter, while Meta Platforms (META:NASDAQ) and Pinterest (PINS:NYSE) kept growing at double-digit rates.

30 million people now pay for Snapchat

Paid subscribers rose 77% to about 30 million in the third quarter, and other revenue, mostly subscriptions, jumped 84% to $350 million. Advertising grew just 4% to $1.37 billion. So subscriptions brought in about three-quarters of the revenue Snap added. Black wrote: "Subscriptions increasingly matter to both the quality of revenue and the margin story, yet we think this remains underappreciated by investors."

Analysts expect revenue to keep climbing through 2028:

Snap (SNAP): revenue, actual and consensus estimates, $ billions, fiscal 2023-2028 (TIKR)

Black sees subscription revenue of about $1.81 billion in 2027, up about 35%, against consensus of roughly 11% growth for the whole company. Gross margin rose from 55.3% a year earlier to 62.3% in the third quarter.

Snap (SNAP): gross margin (%), last 8 quarters (to September 30, 2026) (TIKR)
Snap's ad problem is its own

North American daily users fell 6% to 92 million.

Rivals aren't seeing the same thing. Meta grew third-quarter revenue 26% to $64.6 billion. Pinterest grew 12%. And Reddit grew revenue 53% as its daily users rose 12%. Advertisers are still spending, just less with Snap, which is why subscriptions matter so much.

TIKR tracks 41 analysts on Snap. How many say "Buy"?

See the full breakdown of Buy, Hold, and Sell ratings on Snap, along with Wall Street's revenue and earnings estimates, all in one place. More than 500,000 investors use TIKR to research stocks like this one. See Snap's Analyst Ratings

Cheap, with one big caveat

Black's $8 target is about 60% above Snap's close before today's jump. The stock traded at 6.6x forward earnings at the last close, well under its one-year average of about 12x. But those normalized earnings leave out roughly $1.05 billion of stock pay this year.

title: Snap Is Still Down 34% in 2026: Did Today Mark the Bottom for SNAP Stock?

Quick Read

Snap's swing to profit and 7x forward earnings can't offset 4% ad growth, missed user targets and rising dilution, leaving the stock down 34%.

Meta's 26% ad growth and 4% stock decline show the pain is concentrated in smaller platforms, with Pinterest down 26% alongside Snap.

February's fourth-quarter report will test whether Snap's ad growth rebounds toward double digits and whether it holds its 2027 pledge to stabilize share count.

Read More: Learn 7 ways to generate income with a $1,000,000+ portfolio (sponsor)

A return to profit hasn't been enough to repair a tough year for Snap (NYSE:SNAP). Snap stock has dropped 34% year to date (YTD) to $5.32 in late-day trading. The Snapchat parent is up 6% from the prior close, carried higher by a broad rally in technology stocks.

stockcatalog / Flickr

The bounce raises a fair question for anyone following Snap: is the worst already priced in? Answering that depends on whether Snap's sharply better profitability can outweigh slow advertising growth, mounting legal pressure over youth safety and steady stock dilution.

What Snap's Third-Quarter Report Revealed

Snap stock remains below the $5.56 it traded at when the company filed its Q3 2026 results on November 4. Revenue at Snap rose 14% to $1.72 billion, and the company swung to a profit of $56 million. Underneath, Snap's advertising revenue grew just 4%, as brand campaigns declined from a year earlier while direct-response ads expanded.

CEO Evan Spiegel acknowledged the gap. In the company's release, "While advertising revenue growth remains below our ambitions, advertisers are seeing the benefits of our performance improvements." daily active users totaled 495 million at Snap, missing the 499 million analysts expected.

Paid subscriptions offered a brighter spot, with Snap passing 30 million subscribers across Snapchat+, Memories Storage and Lens+. That subscriber base helped Snap's other revenue climb 84%, while gross margin expanded to 62%.
